summary:
Cauca stands under Colombia's national framework on gender identity and sexual orientation. The national provisions on identification markers, partner recognition, non-discrimination and access to public accommodation are carried by the Colombia record and are not restated here. No Cauca-specific statute, court ruling, administrative order or documented incident appears in the sources assembled for this department.

Human Rights Watch's Colombia page records no finding for Cauca, and the CNN 'As Equals' follow-up of 6 August 2025 on continuing killings of LGBTQ+ people after the Sara Millerey case describes no incident in the department. Neither source offers a departmental breakdown for Cauca, so neither can be read as evidence of conditions here one way or the other.

Armed-group targeting of LGBTI residents is documented in Colombia, but the documented flyer and messaging campaigns are recorded in Caquetá department, not in Cauca. No kill list, named threat or campaign against trans residents in this department appears in the sources. Whether the armed-group pattern extends into Cauca is unresolved, and no Cauca departmental or municipal authority is cited in any of the material.
tangentialFactors:
Comparisons in the sourcing run in one direction only. The armed-group campaigns that named LGBTI people as legitimate military targets are documented in Caquetá, where reported threats forced a trans woman and election candidate to flee and where a second trans woman said a friend had been killed. That material belongs to the Caquetá record. No comparable account exists for Cauca, and its absence is a gap in reporting rather than a documented clean bill of health.

The CNN follow-up is national in scope, tracking continuing killings of LGBTQ+ people and gang involvement across Colombia. It names no department in Cauca and gives no sub-national breakdown, so treating it as a Cauca finding would overstate the evidence. The national killing figures that appear alongside it are carried by the Colombia record.
localsOnly:
No Cauca-specific finding on policing, custody, healthcare, education or employment for trans residents appears in the sources assembled here. The reporting on discrimination that confines trans women mainly to hairdressing or sex work, and on threats that forced a trans woman to leave her town, concerns Caquetá and is carried by that department's record.

No Cauca departmental authority, human rights ombudsman office, municipal programme or local LGBTI organisation is cited in the material, so nothing in it describes how the national decrees and court rulings on prisons, education, health and public premises are applied inside this department.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the armed-group 'social cleansing' pattern documented elsewhere in Colombia reaches Cauca is unresolved. The sources assembled here record no flyer campaign, kill list, named threat or killing in this department, so extending the pattern to Cauca is an inference rather than a documented finding.

Whether Cauca's absence from these sources reflects the absence of incidents or the absence of departmental monitoring and reporting cannot be determined from the material available. No Cauca departmental authority, ombudsman office or local organisation is cited.

National counts of trans and LGBTI people killed are carried by the Colombia record and cannot be converted into a Cauca rate: no Cauca population denominator and no departmental count are available here. Cauca's general homicide rate is not sourced in this inventory, so no comparison between trans-specific and general violence in the department can be made.
